title: SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM): the Admin Console policy page and Advanced SSPM

prose.text: {{what-sspm-is}} {{policy-page-location}} The policies, their statuses and compliance types are in [[zia.sspm.policies]].

prose.label: Advanced SSPM.
prose.text: {{advanced-what}} {{advanced-access}} {{advanced-redirects-to-app-governance}} Its Posture, Control Panel and Compliance pages are in [[zia.sspm.posture]], and the platforms with their own connection pages are in [[zia.sspm.platforms]].

prose.label: Onboarding.
prose.text: The permissions and admin role each SaaS application needs for the SSPM scan are in [[zia.sspm.permissions]]. {{advanced-platforms}} The vendor's pages list the supported applications differently {{divergence:application-lists}}, and whether the lists cover different tiers is open {{gap:list-tiers}}.

prose.label: Licensing.
prose.text: How the Advanced SSPM subscription relates to the 3rd-Party App Governance subscription is open {{gap:license-relationship}}. The sibling product is [[zia.app-governance]].

prose.label: Not this product.
prose.text: Data-at-rest scanning of SaaS files is [[zia.casb]]. Data security posture management is [[dspm.overview]]. The cloud workload posture product is [[portfolio.cloud-protection]].

checks.do: Which tier a question is about, the Admin Console SSPM policy page or Advanced SSPM, before quoting an application list.

what-sspm-is.statement: SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) is the practice of systematically assessing, monitoring and improving the security posture of SaaS applications in an organization, and is described as a collection of recommended security policies.

quotes: SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) refers to the practice of systematically assessing, monitoring, and improving the security posture of SaaS applications within an organization. It is a collection of recommended security policies that are enabled for your business requirements.

policy-page-location.statement: The SSPM policy page in the Zscaler Admin Console is reached from the navigation menu at Data Security > SaaS Security > Posture Management.

quotes: From the navigation menu, go to Data Security > SaaS Security > Posture Management.

advanced-redirects-to-app-governance.statement: If Advanced Posture Management is enabled by a license, the Posture Management page redirects to the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal.

quotes: If you have Advanced Posture Management enabled via a license, the Posture Management page redirects to the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal.

advanced-what.statement: Advanced SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) is described as a unified solution for security across SaaS apps and platforms, from data visibility to posture and governance. It helps identify and mitigate risky misconfigurations, control SaaS sprawl, reduce third-party access and identify users at risk, and lets you vet third-party integrations, revoke risky connections and ensure least-privileged SaaS access.

quotes: Zscaler Advanced SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) is a comprehensive and unified solution that delivers complete security across Software as a Service (SaaS) apps and platforms, from data visibility to posture and governance.
It helps you to quickly identify and mitigate risky misconfigurations, control SaaS sprawl and reduce third-party access, and identify users at risk.

Advanced SSPM lets you reduce your attack surface by vetting third-party integrations and revoking risky connections. You can also ensure least-privileged SaaS access and revoke over privileged identities and permissions.

advanced-access.statement: Subscribers to the Advanced SSPM service reach it from the Zscaler Admin Console with single sign-on, at Analytics > Reports > SaaS Security Report > Posture Management. The Compliance page says that subscribers to the Advanced SSPM service can access it.

quotes: If you subscribe to the Advanced SSPM service, you can access Advanced SSPM from the Zscaler Admin Console using single sign-on (SSO).
To access Advanced SSPM, go to Analytics > Reports > SaaS Security Report > Posture Management.
If you subscribed to the Advanced SSPM service, you can access the Compliance page.

advanced-platforms.statement: Advanced SSPM supports API-based platforms that are onboarded from the Zscaler Admin Console or the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal, listed as Airtable, Bitbucket, Bitwarden, Box, Confluence, Databricks, Docusign, Dropbox, GitHub, GitLab, Google Workspace, Jira, JumpCloud, Lucid, Microsoft 365, Microsoft Copilot, Okta, OneLogin, OpenAI, Oracle Financials Cloud, Salesforce, Sentry, ServiceNow, ShareFile, Slack, Smartsheet, Snowflake, Trello, Twilio, Webex Teams, Workday, Zendesk and Zoom.

quotes: Advanced SSPM supports the following API-based platforms. These platforms are onboarded from the Zscaler Admin Console or the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal.
- Airtable - Bitbucket - Bitwarden - Box - Confluence - Databricks - Docusign - Dropbox - GitHub - GitLab - Google Workspace - Jira - JumpCloud - Lucid

- Microsoft 365 - Microsoft Copilot - Okta - OneLogin - OpenAI - Oracle Financials Cloud - Salesforce - Sentry - ServiceNow - ShareFile - Slack - Smartsheet - Snowflake - Trello - Twilio - Webex Teams - Workday - Zendesk - Zoom

application-lists.summary: The vendor's pages give three different lists of SaaS applications for SSPM: the SSPM policy page, the onboarding permissions page and the Advanced SSPM page.

quotes: You can configure SSPM while onboarding tenants for the following SaaS applications:
- Bitbucket - Confluence - GitHub - Google Workspace - Jira - Microsoft 365 - Okta - Salesforce - ServiceNow

positions.says: The SSPM policy page lists nine applications for configuring SSPM while onboarding tenants: Bitbucket, Confluence, GitHub, Google Workspace, Jira, Microsoft 365, Okta, Salesforce and ServiceNow.

quotes: A user with Administrator privileges is required to onboard Box for SSPM.
An Organization Admin with Full Admin, Compliance Officer, and Webex Site Admin roles is required to onboard Webex Teams for SSPM.
An account owner is required to onboard Zoom for SSPM.

positions.says: The onboarding permissions page has onboarding requirements for applications that include Box, Webex Teams and Zoom, which the policy page does not list.

quotes: Advanced SSPM supports the following API-based platforms. These platforms are onboarded from the Zscaler Admin Console or the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal.
- Smartsheet - Snowflake - Trello - Twilio - Webex Teams - Workday - Zendesk

positions.says: The Advanced SSPM page lists API-based platforms that include Smartsheet, Snowflake, Trello, Twilio, Webex Teams, Workday and Zendesk, which the policy page does not list.

application-lists.impact: An answer about which applications SSPM covers differs by page. Whether the pages describe different tiers is not stated by any of them, so a question has to say which tier and console it concerns.

list-tiers.title: Whether the three SSPM application lists cover different tiers
list-tiers.detail: The SSPM policy page, the onboarding permissions page and the Advanced SSPM page give different application lists. They may describe the Admin Console policy tier and Advanced SSPM separately, but no captured page says which list belongs to which tier.

license-relationship.title: How the Advanced SSPM and 3rd-Party App Governance licenses relate
license-relationship.detail: Advanced SSPM redirects into the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal, and the portal requires its own subscription. The captured pages do not say whether one license covers both, and the 'enterprise tiers' that allow SAML in the portal are not defined. An uncited capture on SSPM licensing and fair use may answer it.
